title: Stock, Warehouses, and Units
readerIntent: Understand balances, availability, sourcing, movement, and measurement.
priorKnowledge: Understand products, warehouses, service areas, and trusted context.
owner: Inventory owns stock; Units owns reusable measurement definitions
summary: Inventory manages pools, warehouse balances, reservations, allocations, movements, transfers, reconciliation, sourcing, and availability using normalized Units contracts.

sections.heading: Inventory model
items: StockPool groups balances for a business purpose without becoming a separate module.
Warehouse balance records on-hand quantity in a normalized unit.
Reservations hold stock; allocations commit fulfillment intent; movements and transfers provide traceable changes.
Availability-to-sell derives from on-hand, reserved, allocated, safety, sellability, scope, and policy.
Reconciliation compares authoritative physical/external evidence with recorded movements and balances.

sections.heading: Ledger, balance, and availability
items: A movement is auditable business evidence that quantity changed; a balance is the current authoritative state derived or maintained under controlled concurrency; availability is a contextual projection for selling.

A reservation temporarily protects quantity for a demand. Allocation records stronger fulfillment intent. Release, expiry, cancellation, shipment, receipt, adjustment, and transfer must use explicit reasons and idempotent commands.
Availability-to-sell must never be treated as a stored universal number when warehouse eligibility, Store, delivery zone, segment, safety stock, or unit conversion can alter the answer.
Optimistic concurrency, idempotency keys, non-negative policies, precision rules, and transaction boundaries prevent retries or parallel orders from silently overselling.

sections.heading: Measurement
items: Quantity/count, mass such as kilogram and gram, volume such as litre and millilitre, length, area, and other configured dimensions.
Land and agricultural inventory can use area units and parcel-specific attributes.
Conversions require compatible dimensions, precision, rounding, canonical units, and audit-friendly original values.
Units is reusable framework data; Inventory owns how measurement affects stock.

sections.heading: Online flow
items: Approved staged Inventory publishes to Online where configured.
Online loads bounded availability projections into NodeCache, Redis, or a qualified provider.
Reads may use cache; successful movements, reservations, releases, transfers, reconciliation, and publication invalidate affected keys.
Cache outage falls back or fails according to channel policy; it never changes authoritative balance.

sections.heading: Measured stock example and operations
items: A grocery warehouse receives 125 kilograms of produce, sells in kilograms and grams, and reserves 750 grams for an order. Units validates dimensional compatibility and conversion precision; Inventory records the original and normalized quantities.

A land or agriculture implementation may use hectares, square metres, parcels, or harvest attributes. The unit definition is reusable, while domain-specific eligibility and stock meaning remain in the owning application capability.

Verify fractional quantities, rounding boundaries, incompatible dimensions, duplicate reservation, concurrent decrement, expiry, transfer in transit, reconciliation variance, staged publication, and cache/search refresh.

Operators monitor negative-balance prevention, aged reservations, failed movements, reconciliation drift, hot warehouse contention, projection lag, provider availability, and correlation identifiers from command through derived reads.
